```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)

```

## Initial Load

Load the sample meters (primary and EV) and take a look at the usage curves.

```{r load}

primaryMeter = read_csv("raw_data/41100_readings_09012026-09182026.corrected.csv")
evMeter = read_csv("raw_data/ZEF2210154531_readings_09012026-09182026.corrected.csv")

# combine start date and start times
primaryMeter$start = paste(primaryMeter$`start-date`, primaryMeter$`start-time`, sep=" ")
evMeter$start = paste(evMeter$`start-date`, evMeter$`start-time`, sep=" ")

# treat as date - thanks Claude
primaryMeter$start = as.POSIXct(primaryMeter$start, format = "%m-%d-%Y %H:%M")
evMeter$start = as.POSIXct(evMeter$start, format = "%m-%d-%Y %H:%M")

```

```{r}

ggplot(data = primaryMeter, aes(x = start, y = value)) + geom_line()

```
```{r}

ggplot(data = evMeter, aes(x = start, y = value)) + geom_line()

```

## One Day

Get a single day's usage to look at a smaller amount of time. Note how the EV meter is 0 most of the time but then shows usage corresponding with when the primary meter also has an uptick. 

### EV demand

```{r}

quarterHour = 7.68/4
fiveMinute = quarterHour/3

```

The lowest amount of demand (kW) on a level 2 EV charger is 7.68 kW - that is a 40 amp charger. In a 15 minute interval the total kWh would be: `quarterHour`. Assuming the charger was not on for the whole 15 minutes a 5 minute increment would be: `fiveMinute`. Safe to assume any usage over 1kWh the EV charger is on, while less than that it's in "idle" state. Idle may use some small amount of power. 


```{r}

singlePrimary = primaryMeter[primaryMeter$`start-date` == '09-02-2026', ]
singleEV = evMeter[evMeter$`start-date` == '09-02-2026', ]

ggplot() + 
  geom_line(data = singlePrimary, aes(x = start, y = value), color = "blue") +
  geom_line(data = singleEV, aes(x = start, y = value), color = "red")
```
